title: Hello, Python
summary: Print text, join values, and meet the f-string.

steps.title: Your first script
body: A Python program is a file of **statements**, run top to bottom. There is no `Main`, no class, no `;`:
```python
print("Hello, World!")
- `print(...)` is a built-in **function**, like `Console.WriteLine` but always available with no `using`.
- Strings take `"double"` or `'single'` quotes; they mean exactly the same thing.
- A line ends the statement. No semicolons.
Comments start with `#` and run to the end of the line.
> **Tip:** coming from C#, the biggest early surprise is that **indentation is syntax**. You will meet it in the next module.

steps.explain: Python is case-sensitive (`Print` does not exist), text needs quotes, and `print` is a plain function. A trailing `;` would actually be allowed, but nobody writes it.

steps.title: Say hello
steps.prompt: Make the program print exactly `Hello, World!`

steps.title: Several values, sep and end
body: `print` takes any number of values and puts a space between them. Two keyword arguments change that:
```python
print("a", "b", "c")            # a b c
print("a", "b", "c", sep="-")   # a-b-c
print("no newline", end="")     # stays on the same line
print("!")                      # no newline!
`sep` is what goes **between** values; `end` is what goes **after** them (default `"\n"`). C#'s `Console.Write` is `print(..., end="")`.

steps.explain: `sep=""` glues `x` and `y`. The second print ends with `.` instead of a newline, so `done` joins the same line.

steps.title: f-strings
body: An **f-string** is C#'s `$"..."` interpolation: put `f` before the quote and expressions in `{}`.
```python
name = "Ada"
year = 1815
print(f"{name} was born in {year}.")
print(f"In 2015 she would be {2015 - year}.")
Any expression works inside the braces. Add `=` to print the expression too, which is handy for debugging: `f"{year=}"` gives `year=1815`.

steps.prompt: Complete the line so it prints `Total: 12`.
steps.explain: Python's interpolation prefix is `f`, and expressions go in curly braces, just like C#.

steps.explain: Each `end=" "` keeps the cursor on the line; the last print supplies the newline.
